subject: Mutual acceptance plan: MAP + test owners, timeline, and exit gates
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual acceptance plan: MAP + test owners, timeline, and exit gates

Liam —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is a first-pass mutual acceptance plan (MAP_v1.xlsx) and a companion list of acceptance test cases. I pulled together what we discussed for success criteria and exit gates so procurement and your engineering team can validate. High level:

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference integration for the Acme Care triage flow with production-like traffic, confirm SLOs and model quality, and unblock contract signature.
- Timeline proposal: 3-week evaluation (canary + ramp) with a final sign-off meeting the week of Aug 25. Detailed dates below.
- Primary success criteria (draft): p95 latency <= 200ms, inference throughput >= 50r/s sustained, semantic recall on the evaluation set >= 0.86, classification accuracy >= 92% on labeled cases, no PII leakage incidents, and SOC2 evidence provided.
- Exit gates: failure to meet any high-severity test (SLOs, data security, or regression >5% vs baseline) will trigger a pause and joint remediation plan.

Can you confirm the owners on your side (engineering and procurement) and whether the timeline looks feasible? Once you confirm, Ben will add the product-level acceptance test owners and Marissa will publish a canary/rollback runbook.

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx (timeline + owner columns), acceptance-test-cases.md

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0147

Subject: Re: Mutual acceptance plan: MAP + test owners, timeline, and exit gates

Thanks Grace — I reviewed the attachments. Overall this looks aligned. A few notes/questions from our side:

1) Procurement: we'll need a slightly compressed timeline for contract review (we're aiming to sign by Sep 1). Procurement is copied; they asked for the final MAP and a single consolidated attachment with acceptance criteria we can include in the SOW.
2) Security: our security team requires SOC2 Type II report and a short evidence bundle (data retention, KMS usage, and access logs) before production sign-off. Can Redwood provide those artifacts during the canary?
3) Evaluation data: we'll provide a 10k-sample labeled set (de-identified) for the accuracy and recall checks; engineering will run inference against it and share results.

Owners on our side: myself (eng lead), Sara Patel (engineering manager, sara@acmehealth.com), and Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>. Timeline: compressed is fine — can we start the canary Aug 12 and aim for a sign-off meeting Aug 26?

Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Aug 2025 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual acceptance plan: MAP + test owners, timeline, and exit gates

Copying product/ops to lock acceptance thresholds. Based on the proposed evaluation we should be explicit about test types, pass/fail thresholds, and who runs each test:

- Performance (run by Redwood ops during canary): p50/p95/p99 latency breakdown, throughput sustained at target concurrency. Acceptance = p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 400ms during steady-state windows.
- Quality (run by Acme + Redwood QA): classification accuracy >= 92% on the provided labeled set; semantic recall >= 0.86 (cosine-based) for top-5 retrieval. Statistical significance target: 95% CI on metrics.
- Regression signal (automated): no more than 5% relative drop in accuracy vs baseline on holdout test. If regression >5% then the gate fails.
- Security & compliance (joint): SOC2 evidence delivered and spot-check access logs and retention policies reviewed. Failure = any missing artifacts or unresolved findings rated medium/high.

Marissa — can you own the canary release runbook and define the automated smoke tests and rollback conditions? I'll draft the acceptance-test-cases.md with specific test commands and metrics exporters.

Ben
Ben Carter
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmehealth.com>, Sara Patel <sara@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Aug 2025 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual acceptance plan: MAP + test owners, timeline, and exit gates

Ben — happy to own the canary runbook. I've updated acceptance-test-cases.md to include owners and automated checks. Key items now in the doc:

- Canary window: Aug 12 00:00 PDT — Aug 19 23:59 PDT (7 days), followed by ramp to 25% production traffic Aug 20-24.
- Go/No-go gate for canary -> ramp: all high-severity smoke tests green for 6 consecutive hours and p95 latency target met for two 1-hour windows.
- Rollback conditions: any of the following sustained for 10 minutes triggers automatic rollback to baseline: error rate > 5% (5xx or client failures), p95 latency > 350ms, or production CPU/GPU saturation > 85%. See canary-rollback-conditions.png.
- Acceptance test runbook: nightly automated quality sweep against the 10k labeled set; PR/CI hooks to run regression checks on model updates.
- Owners: Marissa (canary ops), Ben (test artifacts + dashboards), Grace (customer PO), Sara (Acme test lead).

I'll post the updated runbook and a short checklist (owner sign-offs required) to the Drive link. If everyone is aligned I'll create a shared calendar invite for an Aug 26 sign-off meeting (30 minutes) and a pre-cutover rehearsal Aug 19.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Mutual acceptance plan: MAP + test owners, timeline, and exit gates — final confirmation

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Final summary / decisions made (for the SOW appendix):

1) Timeline:
   - Canary start: 2025-08-12
   - Canary end / rehearsal: 2025-08-19
   - Ramp window: 2025-08-20 to 2025-08-24 (incremental traffic increases)
   - Final sign-off meeting: 2025-08-26 (30 minutes)

2) Metrics & success criteria:
   - p95 latency <= 200ms (acceptance) / rollback threshold p95 > 350ms
   - p99 latency <= 400ms
   - Throughput: sustain >= 50 reqs/sec at target concurrency
   - Quality: classification accuracy >= 92% on Acme labeled set; semantic recall >= 0.86 (top-5)
   - Regression: <5% relative drop vs baseline on holdout set
   - Security: SOC2 Type II report + evidence bundle delivered during canary

3) Owners: Grace (customer PO), Marissa (canary ops / runbook), Ben (acceptance test artifacts + dashboards), Sara (Acme test lead), Liam (Acme eng lead), Procurement (contracting).

4) Attachments to be bundled with SOW: MAP_v1.xlsx (timeline + responsibilities), acceptance-test-cases.md (detailed tests + pass/fail), canary-rollback-conditions.png, SOC2_evidence_checklist.docx (placeholder).

5) Next steps: Marissa will publish the runbook by EOD Aug 8; Ben will share the test artifact repo and a Prometheus dashboard link; Grace to confirm the Aug 26 meeting invite once procurement confirms contract cadence.

If no objections by EOD Aug 11 I'll mark this MAP as the agreed appendix for the SOW and share the combined PDF for procurement.

Best,
Grace
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
